newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Syria's Assad says Netanyahu obliterating peace.
newsitem.headline: Syria's Assad says Netanyahu obliterating peace.

text.p: Syrian President Hafez al-Assad said in a U.S. television interview that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu appears to be "obliterating" peace commitments made by the previous Israeli Labour government.

"Once the results of the Israeli elections were announced, the new Israeli Prime Minister appeared to be obliterating all the principles and eliminating all efforts, commitments and rights. And so he cancelled the peace process entirely," Assad told CNN International in an interview to be aired on Saturday.
"Talks can only be resumed once he makes up his mind on the peace strategy and on responding to its requirements."
"He (Netanyahu) is blocking the roads towards peace," Assad said in excerpts made available by CNN on Friday.
Assad said that stability in the Middle East will diminish if negotiations are not resumed between Israel and Syria and this could lead to war.
"Changes in this stability could lead to what we may call war or wars," the Syrian President said in his first U.S. and European television interview since 1993.
But he said that the peace process was not dead but only "stumbling."

Assad disclosed after years of public denials that Israel's former Labour government and Syria had reached in four years of negotiations an agreement on Israeli withdrawal from the Syrian Golan Heights, captured by Israel in June 1967.
Netanyahu won May elections on a platform opposed to trading occupied Arab land for peace.

"Agreement was reached between Syria and Israel on Israeli withdrawal from the Golan up to June 4, 1967 lines. After that we moved to complete discussion of the other elements of peace. And all that took place under the supervision and with the knowledge of the United States," he said.

No peace talks have been held between Israel and Syria since the May election of Netanyahu as prime minister. Netanyahu rejects the land-for-peace formula and supports the increase of Jewish settlements in the occupied Arab lands.
Syria, which has held sporadic peace talks with Israel since 1991, wants Netanyahu to announce readiness to withdraw fully from the Golan ahead of any resumption of negotiations.
